items.question:
A CISO at a 2,000-person professional services firm asks why, if the company has SSO configured for Claude.ai, the engineering team still needs to manage API keys for the firm's internally built Claude-powered tools.

What is the correct explanation?

options.A: SSO manages employee identity for Claude.ai human sessions; API keys authenticate server-to-server calls made by the firm's own applications — they operate at different layers and serve different purposes
options.B: SSO replaces API keys entirely; once SSO is configured, all Claude access — including programmatic API calls — routes through the identity provider
options.C: API keys are required only during development; in production, the SSO token takes over as the API authentication mechanism
options.D: SSO does not support technical users; engineers require API keys because SSO configuration only provisions business-role employees

items.question:
A programme director at a 400-person logistics company asks the consultant for both a model tier recommendation and a cost estimate for a Claude-powered shipment exception alert system before the business case goes to the board. Representative sample exception data is available.

In what order should the consultant address these two deliverables?

options.A: Estimate cost first using the highest-tier model to produce a conservative upper-bound figure, then recommend that tier to the board
options.B: Test sample exception alerts through each tier starting with Haiku to establish the minimum tier that meets quality requirements, then build the cost estimate using that tier's rate and expected volume
options.C: Provide a cost estimate based on assumed Sonnet usage, then adjust the tier recommendation to fit the programme director's budget tolerance
options.D: Request a 30-day pilot budget to run both tiers in parallel before making either recommendation

items.question:
A digital lead at a European pharmaceutical company needs Claude for clinical trial data summarisation. The security team has confirmed EU data residency is required. The finance team asks whether the cloud marketplace route is always more expensive than the direct Anthropic API, and whether cost should factor into the deployment route decision.

What is the MOST accurate response?

options.A: Cloud marketplace deployments always carry a significant premium; the company should negotiate a data residency exception to use the cheaper direct API
options.B: Cloud marketplace pricing may be comparable or bundled within existing cloud commitments; more importantly, the residency requirement is not a cost trade-off — the correct frame is which compliant option is most cost-effective
options.C: Install a VPN proxy in the EU that intercepts API traffic before forwarding to Anthropic, satisfying residency at lower cost than a marketplace deployment
options.D: Direct API and cloud marketplace pricing are identical because Anthropic controls per-token rates centrally

items.question:
An operations VP at a manufacturing company tells the engineering team: "Claude keeps giving vague answers about safety procedures. Build a retrieval system to give it more context." The team spends three months building a retrieval-augmented system. Output quality does not improve. A consultant is called in.

What was the fundamental failure in how this problem was approached?

options.A: The retrieval system used the wrong indexing approach; a different document retrieval architecture would have produced better results
options.B: The VP should have requested a fine-tuned model rather than a retrieval system, as fine-tuning is more effective for domain-specific language
options.C: The engineering team needed a larger budget to complete a higher-quality retrieval implementation
options.D: A solution was specified before the root cause was identified; a brief prompt engineering test would have determined whether the problem was missing context or unclear instructions, potentially avoiding three months of misdirected effort

items.question:
A startup CTO argues that since the engineering team uses Claude Code, requirements documentation is unnecessary — Claude Code can figure out what to build from a brief description.

What should the consultant say?

options.A: Claude Code accelerates implementation given clear instructions but cannot replace requirements documentation — it needs to know what to build, which requires human clarity about intended behaviour and acceptance criteria
options.B: The CTO is correct; Claude Code's autonomous capabilities allow it to infer full requirements from a business context description
options.C: Requirements documentation is only necessary for offshore teams; co-located teams using Claude Code can rely on verbal alignment
options.D: Claude Code generates its own requirements documentation automatically before writing code, so the team only needs to review rather than write specifications

items.question:
A technology director at a 1,500-employee retail bank discovers 80 analysts using personal Claude.ai accounts for work tasks. Most are finding genuine productivity value. The director wants to convert this shadow use into a sanctioned program rather than banning it.

What is the MOST effective approach?

options.A: Issue a blanket ban with disciplinary consequences and evaluate sanctioned options on a six-month review timeline
options.B: Negotiate an enterprise Claude.ai agreement with appropriate data handling terms, migrate users via SSO, and use the analysts' existing workflows to seed the prompt library and governance policy
options.C: Allow personal account use to continue with a mandatory data disclosure form so IT can monitor what types of information are being processed
options.D: Run a five-analyst pilot for twelve months to build evidence before expanding to the broader population

items.question:
A pipeline engineering manager at a 300-person media company reports that a Claude-powered content tagging tool hits rate limit errors during editorial publishing peaks. A developer suggests switching from Sonnet to Haiku because a faster model would process requests more quickly and avoid the limits.

What is the most accurate response to the developer's suggestion?

options.A: The developer is correct — Haiku's lower latency means individual requests complete faster, creating more room in the rate limit window
options.B: The developer is partially correct — Haiku reduces token spend per call, which helps the token-per-minute component of rate limiting
options.C: The developer's reasoning conflates call latency with rate limit capacity — rate limits constrain requests per minute and tokens per minute at the account level, not the speed of individual responses. Switching tiers does not increase the account's request allowance
options.D: The developer is correct — Haiku generates shorter outputs, consuming less of the rate limit budget per request and allowing more total requests before the limit is hit

items.question:
A global asset manager deploys Claude.ai for 600 portfolio analysts (SSO-provisioned) and simultaneously operates a Claude API integration embedded in their risk management platform. The CISO asks whether the SSO configuration that governs analyst access also protects the API integration.

What is the correct answer?

options.A: Yes — once SSO is configured at the account level, all access including API calls routes through the identity provider
options.B: Yes — SSO covers user sessions; for API calls, the identity provider token is automatically passed as the API authentication credential
options.C: Partially — SSO governs analyst access; a separate rate-limiting rule must be added for the API integration
options.D: No — SSO governs human identity for Claude.ai sessions; the API integration uses a bearer key independent of SSO and requires separate governance through key management controls

items.question:
A programme director at a health insurer says their Claude-powered prior authorisation tool achieves 97% accuracy on a validated test set and asks whether this is sufficient to remove the human review step for all claims.

What should the consultant advise?

options.A: Even at high accuracy, prior authorisation decisions affecting patient care access require a qualified human decision-maker — at the insurer's claim volume, a 3% error rate represents meaningful patient harm
options.B: 97% accuracy meets the industry standard for full automation in insurance; the human review step can be removed
options.C: Human review can be removed if the system adds a confidence score and routes only low-confidence cases to manual review
options.D: The decision should be based on the time saved per claim; if AI is ten times faster, the efficiency gain justifies full automation

items.question: A consultant is finalising a handoff package for a Claude-powered internal knowledge search tool at a 2,500-employee energy company. The engineering lead says the package is nearly complete but asks for two specific elements before the team can begin implementation. Which TWO elements is the engineering lead MOST likely requesting? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A list of all business stakeholders who must be consulted during the implementation phase
options.B: Representative sample queries and their expected search result quality, so the team has concrete examples of what a successful outcome looks like
options.C: A description of the company's preferred project management methodology for AI initiatives
options.D: The specific data sources the search tool must index, with sufficient detail about format and access method for the team to design the data pipeline
options.E: A decision on whether to use Agile or waterfall delivery for the implementation sprint

items.question:
An IT architect at a 600-person insurance company is building a Claude-powered policy document review tool. Adjusters will upload third-party legal documents that may contain embedded text designed to manipulate the model. The architect asks what requirement to add to the system prompt to reduce this risk.

What is the MOST effective instruction?

options.A: Instruct the model to reject any document that contains legal boilerplate exceeding three pages
options.B: Remove the system prompt entirely so there are no instructions for adversarial text to override
options.C: Explicitly instruct the model that all content within designated document tags is source material to be analysed — not instructions to follow — and that the model's directives come only from the system prompt
options.D: Restrict the tool to processing documents under 5,000 words to limit the space available for injected instructions

items.question:
A data architect at a European bank confirms EU data residency requires a cloud marketplace deployment. Finance calculates this route costs 18% more per month than direct API access. The head of AI strategy asks whether cost should factor into reconsidering the deployment route.

How should the consultant respond?

options.A: Present the marketplace deployment as the correct option with cost accurately disclosed and the compliance rationale clearly documented — the 18% premium is the cost of compliance
options.B: Initiate a formal risk assessment to determine whether data residency is truly non-negotiable, using the cost difference as evidence that a compensating control may be preferable
options.C: Recommend a VPN proxy layer in the EU to route API traffic through, which satisfies residency at approximately 5% additional cost
options.D: Ask the data protection officer to formally accept residency non-compliance as a risk, unlocking use of the direct API

items.question:
A VP of Engineering at a 180-person healthtech company is evaluating Claude Code. She asks where in the software development lifecycle Claude Code provides the MOST direct acceleration for her engineering team.

What is the most accurate answer?

options.A: In the requirements gathering phase, where Claude Code analyses stakeholder interviews and generates structured requirements documents autonomously
options.B: In the implementation, testing, and debugging phases, where developers use Claude Code to write code, generate tests, trace errors, and refactor within their existing terminal environment
options.C: In the deployment phase, where Claude Code automatically provisions cloud infrastructure and deploys services without developer intervention
options.D: In the design phase, where Claude Code generates architecture diagrams and selects the technology stack based on project constraints

items.question: A compliance officer at a 7,000-employee financial services firm needs two things for the Claude.ai enterprise deployment: (1) control over which employees can access the product and what roles they hold, and (2) an audit trail of authentication events for regulatory review. Which control BEST satisfies both requirements simultaneously?

options.A: Per-department admins who manually approve access requests and maintain a shared spreadsheet log of access grants and revocations
options.B: IP allowlisting restricted to corporate network addresses, with firewall logs providing the access audit trail
options.C: SSO integration that ties Claude.ai access to the corporate identity provider, which manages roles and generates a tamper-evident authentication event log
options.D: A shared department login with a quarterly password rotation, with IT logging all login timestamps

items.question:
A business analyst drafts a requirements document for a Claude-powered contract analysis feature that includes the line: "Must use Sonnet model." The engineering lead says this creates a problem. The consultant is asked to explain why.

What is the BEST explanation?

options.A: Specifying a model tier in requirements is appropriate — it removes ambiguity and ensures the team does not choose an underpowered tier
options.B: The Sonnet model cannot be specified in a requirements document; model tier selection is an Anthropic decision, not a client decision
options.C: Specifying Sonnet by default is over-engineering; the requirements document should specify Opus since higher tiers always produce better results for professional analysis
options.D: Model tier is an implementation decision that belongs with the engineering team; the requirements document should define the output quality bar and let the team select the minimum tier that meets it within cost constraints

items.question: A technology architect is designing governance controls for a new Claude API deployment that will serve 15 business units at a 50,000-employee insurance group. The security steering committee asks which TWO controls are MOST critical for enterprise-scale API governance across multiple business units. (Choose TWO)

options.A: A centralised secrets management vault that issues API keys to services rather than individuals, with access audit logs showing which service retrieved each key and when
options.B: A mandatory AI training course for all 50,000 employees before any API access is granted
options.C: Per-business-unit usage monitoring with spend attribution and automated alerts when a unit's consumption deviates significantly from its established baseline
options.D: A policy requiring all API calls to include the user's employee ID in the request header for individual-level attribution
options.E: A six-month pilot restricted to three business units before expanding governance controls to the full 15-unit deployment

items.question:
A business unit manager at a logistics company notices that the Claude-powered shipment summary tool is consistently adding legal disclaimers to every summary, even internal operational ones. She is not sure whether to contact the tool's engineering team or the prompt author.

Who should she contact FIRST?

options.A: The cloud infrastructure team, as the disclaimer language is likely inserted by a security layer in the middleware
options.B: The prompt author or the person who configured the tool's system prompt, as consistent disclaimer language in all outputs is a prompt configuration issue
options.C: The engineering team, as the API is likely returning modified responses due to a processing error in the response handler
options.D: Anthropic support, as Claude is inserting disclaimers based on a default safety policy that cannot be changed through the system prompt

items.question: A consultant is advising a 900-person retail bank on which Claude deployment route to select. The bank's team has not yet made any deployment decisions. Which TWO questions MUST be answered before a deployment route recommendation can be made responsibly? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Does the bank have a preference for Python or Node.js for the API integration layer?
options.B: Does the bank's regulatory environment impose any data residency requirements for AI inference?
options.C: Does the bank's leadership prefer an Agile or waterfall delivery approach for the AI programme?
options.D: Will the Claude integration need to process data classified as confidential or regulated (e.g., customer account data, transaction records) within the AI call?
options.E: Does the bank have a preference for the colour scheme of the AI tool's user interface?

items.question: A finance lead at a 300-person asset management firm asks the consultant to estimate monthly Claude API cost for a planned document analysis pipeline. The consultant does not yet have enough information to produce a credible estimate. Which TWO questions should the consultant ask FIRST to make the estimate possible? (Choose TWO)

options.A: What is the expected monthly volume of documents to be processed, and what is the typical length (page count or approximate word count) of the documents?
options.B: Has the finance lead approved the budget for an enterprise data handling agreement with Anthropic?
options.C: What model tier is planned for the pipeline — Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus — or alternatively, what quality bar must the output meet so the consultant can identify the minimum viable tier?
options.D: Does the team plan to use Agile or waterfall delivery for the pipeline implementation?
options.E: Does the finance lead have a preference for monthly or quarterly billing from Anthropic?

items.question: A business owner at a 1,800-employee telecoms company reports that a Claude-powered customer complaint classification tool is producing wrong category labels 25% of the time. She has already instructed the engineering team to upgrade to a more powerful model tier AND rewrite the system prompt simultaneously. A consultant is brought in and pauses both changes. What should happen NEXT?

options.A: Proceed with the model upgrade first and hold the prompt rewrite until the upgrade's effect can be measured
options.B: Proceed with the prompt rewrite first and hold the model upgrade until the rewrite's effect can be measured
options.C: Proceed with both changes simultaneously and measure whether the combined intervention reduces the 25% error rate
options.D: Sample a set of the 25% incorrectly classified complaints and compare them to correctly classified ones to identify what the failing examples have in common before making any change

items.question: A customer experience manager at a telecoms company receives 3,000 support ticket comments per month across 12 product categories. Her team currently reads a sample of 200 tickets manually to produce a monthly theme report. She is considering using Claude to process all 3,000 tickets. Which statement BEST describes where Claude adds genuine leverage in this use case?

options.A: Claude can respond directly to the 3,000 customers, resolving their issues without human involvement
options.B: Claude can process all 3,000 tickets to identify themes and frequency patterns, giving the team a complete-coverage report instead of a 6.7% sample
options.C: Claude can train itself on the ticket data to improve its classification accuracy over time
options.D: Claude can replace the customer experience manager's role in deciding which issues to escalate to product teams

items.question: A bid manager at a professional services firm wants to integrate Claude into the proposal development workflow. The full workflow has six phases: (1) opportunity identification, (2) go/no-go decision, (3) solution design, (4) writing and content assembly, (5) commercial pricing, and (6) internal review and sign-off. Which TWO phases represent the STRONGEST fit for Claude assistance, and which option correctly identifies them?

options.A: Phases 1 and 2, because opportunity identification and go/no-go decisions are the most strategic phases where Claude's language ability adds the most value
options.B: Phases 3 and 5, because solution design and pricing require the deepest analytical thinking
options.C: Phases 4 and 6, because writing/assembly and internal review involve large volumes of text that Claude can draft, structure, and check efficiently
options.D: Phases 2 and 5, because go/no-go and pricing decisions follow defined criteria that Claude can evaluate objectively

items.question: A talent acquisition lead at a 90,000-person global manufacturer is reviewing AI use proposals. One proposal is to have Claude independently rank and recommend candidates for senior director roles based on their CV, a competency framework, and the job description. The talent lead rejects the proposal without redesign. What is the PRIMARY reason?

options.A: Claude cannot read PDF-format CVs, so the inputs would not be in a compatible format
options.B: Senior director selection requires judgment about leadership potential, culture fit, and contextual factors that are not fully captured in a CV or competency framework
options.C: The company's ATS system does not integrate with Claude, so data transfer would be manual
options.D: A competency framework is a proprietary document that should not be shared with an AI system

items.question: A programme manager at a public health agency is using Claude to help produce an annual surveillance report. The workflow includes: (A) analysing epidemiological data tables, (B) drafting the methods section from the study protocol, (C) writing the executive summary, (D) copyediting the final document, and (E) translating the executive summary into three languages. Which pair of steps can MOST safely run in PARALLEL?

options.A: Steps A and B, because neither requires the other's output
options.B: Steps B and C, because both involve writing and can be drafted at the same time
options.C: Steps C and D, because the executive summary and copyediting are both post-analysis tasks
options.D: Steps D and E, because both are performed on completed text and neither changes the content

items.question: A data governance analyst at a 5,000-person financial services firm is evaluating whether Claude can assist with data dictionary maintenance. The team reviews 80 database tables per quarter, checking that each column's definition, data type, and business owner are documented. Currently two analysts spend a week per quarter on this. Which property of this task is the STRONGEST fit signal?

options.A: The task is performed quarterly, which is a predictable enough cadence to schedule a batch run
options.B: The team has two analysts available who can review Claude's output before submitting updates to the data dictionary
options.C: Each column check applies the same three criteria — definition, data type, business owner — uniformly across all 80 tables, making the task structurally identical for every instance
options.D: The task is important enough that investing in prompt engineering is justified

items.question: A communications director at a non-profit is preparing for a live Q&A at a funder conference. She wants to use Claude to help her practice responses to likely questions. Her colleague suggests running a batch of 30 probable questions through Claude at once and printing the answers as a reference sheet. Why is INTERACTIVE mode a better choice for this preparation task?

options.A: Interactive mode allows Claude to search the internet for the most current funding landscape information
options.B: Batch mode produces 30 identical-format answers while interactive mode can vary the register and length of each response
options.C: Practising responses is a performance skill that improves through iterative feedback — follow-up questions, tone adjustments, and refinements based on how a draft answer feels are only possible in interactive mode
options.D: Claude produces higher-quality answers when the conversation history includes prior turns rather than starting fresh for each question

items.question: A financial controller at a 200-person manufacturing firm is designing a month-end close workflow with Claude assistance. She proposes four Claude-assisted steps: (1) reconcile bank statement to GL entries by matching transaction IDs, (2) draft the journal entry explanations for unusual variances, (3) calculate the correct accrual amounts for unbilled services, and (4) prepare a summary of open intercompany balances. After review, the CFO rejects one step as misclassified. Which step is MOST likely to be misclassified as Claude-assisted?

options.A: Step 1, because bank reconciliation involves matching transactions that require live access to the bank system and the GL
options.B: Step 2, because drafting journal entry explanations is a creative writing task rather than a financial analysis task
options.C: Step 3, because calculating accrual amounts requires applying accounting judgments about completeness and measurement that have audit and regulatory implications
options.D: Step 4, because summarising intercompany balances is too simple to justify a Claude-assisted step

items.question: A knowledge management lead at a consulting firm is building a workflow to ingest and index 400 project archive documents into a searchable knowledge base. The workflow has four planned steps: (1) classify each document by service line and document type, (2) extract key entities (client name, project dates, methodology), (3) generate a 100-word summary for each document, and (4) build the search index. Her colleague suggests adding a step to have Claude enrich each summary with links to related documents before the index is built. At what point in the workflow is this enrichment step MOST appropriately placed?

options.A: Before step 1, so that the classification can take related-document context into account
options.B: Between steps 3 and 4, after all summaries are generated but before the index is built — so Claude has the full corpus of summaries to reference when identifying relationships
options.C: After step 4, so that the enrichment can use the completed index to surface relationships algorithmically
options.D: Simultaneously with step 3, so that Claude generates the summary and relationships in a single pass for each document

items.question: An HR business partner at a 600-person pharmaceutical company is designing a performance review support workflow. The workflow includes: drafting talking-point templates for managers, summarising 360 feedback comments into themes, generating a development plan from competency gaps, and making a final rating recommendation for each employee. How should these four steps be classified?

options.A: All four steps are Claude-assisted because they are all text-based HR tasks
options.B: The first three steps are Claude-assisted; the final rating recommendation is a human step because it carries employment and compensation consequences
options.C: Only the first step (drafting talking-point templates) is Claude-assisted; all other steps involve individual employee data and require a human
options.D: The first two steps are Claude-assisted; steps 3 and 4 both require a human because they involve individual employees' careers

items.question: A brand manager at a consumer goods company is using Claude to produce a set of 15 product launch assets: a press release, 8 social posts, a retailer one-pager, 4 email templates, and a FAQ document. She plans to draft the press release first and use it as the source of truth for all other assets. What sequencing constraint does this impose on the rest of the batch?

options.A: None — all 15 assets are independent and can be generated simultaneously without a source-of-truth document
options.B: The 14 downstream assets must be generated after the press release is finalised, because they depend on its product positioning and key messages
options.C: Only the social posts must follow the press release; the other assets can be drafted in advance
options.D: The assets should be generated in reverse order — FAQ first, then email templates, then the press release

items.question: A legal counsel at a mid-size technology company is designing a workflow for reviewing non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) submitted by prospective partners. The company receives 60–80 NDAs per month, each 8–15 pages. Which TWO workflow steps represent appropriate Claude-assisted roles that preserve legal accountability? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Extracting and summarising the key terms of each NDA (governing law, limitation period, definition of confidential information) into a structured comparison table
options.B: Flagging clauses that deviate from the company's standard NDA template and annotating the deviation type
options.C: Executing the NDA on behalf of the company and filing the signed copy in the contract management system
options.D: Issuing a final legal sign-off that the NDA is approved for signature without attorney review
options.E: Redlining the NDA with suggested edits to bring non-standard clauses closer to the company's preferred language

items.question: A strategy analyst at a private equity firm evaluates portfolio companies quarterly. Each evaluation requires: reading 20–30 pages of management reports, comparing KPIs against the investment thesis, identifying risks, and producing an investment committee memo. She wants to use Claude throughout this workflow. For which part of this workflow is Claude LEAST suited as the primary author?

options.A: Summarising the 20–30 page management reports into a structured brief
options.B: Extracting and formatting the KPI tables from the reports into a comparison view against the investment thesis targets
options.C: Drafting the investment committee memo based on the analyst's notes and findings
options.D: Assessing whether the identified risks represent a fundamental change to the investment thesis, warranting a hold or exit recommendation

items.question: A VP of Patient Services at a 20-hospital health system is reviewing a proposal to use Claude to assist with patient discharge communication. The proposal includes two use cases: (A) generating standardised discharge instruction summaries from nursing notes, and (B) automatically sending those summaries to patients via the patient portal without clinical staff review. Which TWO design changes would MOST improve the governance of this workflow? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Require a qualified clinical staff member to review and approve the discharge summary before it is sent to the patient
options.B: Replace Claude with a larger model to improve the clinical accuracy of the discharge summaries
options.C: Add a patient acknowledgement step so the patient confirms receipt of the summary
options.D: Limit the discharge summary to only include information that was explicitly present in the nursing notes, with no inference or synthesis
options.E: Log every generated summary with a timestamp so the organisation can audit which patients received which instructions

items.question:
A logistics company receives 800 freight invoices per week, each requiring extraction of the same five fields: carrier name, shipment date, origin, destination, and billed amount. The operations lead is evaluating whether Claude should handle this extraction.

What is the MOST significant factor indicating this is a high-fit task?

options.A: The invoices come from different carriers and use varied layouts.
options.B: The same five-field extraction logic applies to every invoice regardless of source.
options.C: The operations team currently spends two hours per day on manual extraction.
options.D: The company uses a cloud-based ERP that can ingest structured data.

items.question:
An HR business partner asks whether Claude is suited to produce initial screening summaries for 200 job applications. Each summary would assess the applicant against the same six hiring criteria drawn from the job description, which is supplied alongside each resume.

Which characteristic makes this the STRONGEST argument for task fit?

options.A: The applications were submitted through an applicant tracking system.
options.B: The hiring panel will make the final selection decision.
options.C: Each summary applies the same six criteria to a different input document.
options.D: The posting attracted above-average application volume this cycle.

items.question:
A clinical operations coordinator at a diagnostic lab proposes configuring Claude to automatically send patients their test results via the patient portal, with no human review before each message is dispatched.

Why should this specific workflow NOT be implemented as designed?

options.A: Claude cannot send messages through patient portal APIs without a custom integration.
options.B: Diagnostic results require clinical interpretation before patient communication, making unreviewed auto-dispatch inappropriate.
options.C: Sending individual messages is a low-volume task unlikely to justify automation investment.
options.D: Patient portals already have notification features, so Claude adds no value here.

items.question:
A content strategist needs to write a thought-leadership article. Before drafting can begin, she must interview the company's CTO to gather proprietary product insights that are not documented anywhere. The article will incorporate those insights directly.

This task is BEST characterised as:

options.A: Batch work, because multiple articles will eventually be produced for the same publication.
options.B: Inappropriate for Claude, because thought-leadership writing requires human creativity.
options.C: Interactive work, because the inputs required to begin drafting cannot be predetermined and must be gathered in real time.
options.D: A high-fit batch task, because Claude excels at long-form structured writing.

items.question:
A procurement specialist has a 300-page supplier RFP she must screen against 12 vendor criteria. She will make the final selection decision herself based on the screening results.

Where does Claude add the MOST leverage in this workflow?

options.A: Making the final vendor selection based on the screening criteria.
options.B: Drafting the 12-point vendor criteria from scratch without input from the specialist.
options.C: Sending rejection notices to unsuccessful vendors automatically after the decision.
options.D: Reading the 300-page document and flagging which sections address each of the 12 criteria.

items.question: An internal auditor is assessing which audit-support tasks are suitable for Claude assistance. Which TWO characteristics most strongly indicate that a task is a good fit? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The task output will be reviewed by a qualified professional before any action is taken.
options.B: The task requires judgement based on undocumented institutional knowledge specific to one client.
options.C: The task involves applying the same evaluation logic to a large number of similar input documents.
options.D: The task has never been attempted before in the organisation.
options.E: The task currently takes the team fewer than 30 minutes per week to complete manually.

items.question:
A RevOps lead wants to semi-automate her team's monthly account health report. The workflow includes: pulling structured CRM data for each account, scoring each account on four predefined metrics, writing a 2-sentence commentary per account, and flagging at-risk accounts for a human review call.

Which step should remain a HUMAN step?

options.A: Pulling structured CRM data for each account.
options.B: Scoring accounts on the four defined metrics.
options.C: Writing the 2-sentence commentary per account.
options.D: Deciding which flagged accounts warrant escalation to a client call.

items.question:
A legal operations analyst reviews 50 contracts per month. Each requires a legal opinion on whether a novel indemnity clause creates liability under a jurisdiction-specific statute — and the relevant statute changes in scope annually through regulatory guidance.

What is the PRIMARY reason this task is a POOR fit for unsupervised Claude assistance?

options.A: The task requires current jurisdictional legal interpretation that changes over time, not stable pattern application.
options.B: 50 contracts per month is too low a volume to justify investment in AI assistance.
options.C: Contract review tasks fall outside Claude's permitted areas of application.
options.D: Claude cannot process contracts longer than a single document upload.

items.question:
A bid manager at a professional services firm asks Claude to evaluate whether the firm should bid on a $4 million government tender, then draft and submit the bid to the portal without any further human review.

Which aspect of this workflow design is MOST problematic?

options.A: Government tenders are too complex for AI-assisted drafting of any kind.
options.B: The bid value is below the threshold where AI assistance is cost-effective for bid work.
options.C: Claude lacks API access to government submission portals.
options.D: An unreviewed autonomous submission removes human accountability from a high-stakes external commitment on behalf of the firm.

items.question:
An L&D manager is building a compliance training module using Claude. Her planned sequence is: (1) Claude drafts the content, (2) subject-matter experts sign off on accuracy, (3) Claude formats the approved content into a slide deck, (4) the deck is published to the LMS.

A colleague suggests moving step 3 before step 2. What is the BEST argument for keeping the ORIGINAL sequence?

options.A: Formatting before SME review wastes effort if content changes require the slides to be reformatted.
options.B: Claude generates better slide layouts when working from content that has been formally approved.
options.C: SMEs prefer reviewing raw text drafts over formatted slides and give more useful feedback on unformatted content.
options.D: The LMS ingestion process requires a text file as input, not a formatted slide deck.

items.question:
A grant writer at an environmental non-profit must tailor funding proposals to each of 15 foundations. Each proposal requires adjusting the theory-of-change narrative and budget justification to match that foundation's specific published priorities and funding focus areas.

Should this work be treated as batch or interactive, and why?

options.A: Batch, because 15 proposals is a repeatable volume of similar documents.
options.B: Interactive, because each proposal requires a separate prompt with foundation-specific context that must be individually supplied.
options.C: Batch, because all proposals share the same organisation mission statement and core programme description.
options.D: Interactive, because grant writing is a creative task that Claude handles better in conversational turns.

items.question:
An actuarial analyst is building a workflow to produce monthly reserve estimates. She has completed two steps: (1) documented the calculation logic in a shared reference file, and (2) validated a prompt that correctly extracts input values from the monthly data exports. Her next planned step is to have Claude generate the reserve estimate narrative from those extracted values.

What should she do NEXT before proceeding to narrative generation?

options.A: Validate Claude's extracted values against the system-of-record figures before using them as narrative inputs.
options.B: Publish the extraction prompt to the wider actuarial team so others can replicate the workflow.
options.C: Switch to a higher-tier model for the narrative generation step to ensure numerical precision.
options.D: Schedule the full workflow to run automatically at month-end without additional testing.

items.question: A supply chain analyst is mapping her supplier onboarding process to identify where Claude can assist. Which TWO steps are MOST appropriate for Claude assistance? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Drafting a standard supplier questionnaire based on the team's defined information requirements.
options.B: Approving a supplier's credit terms on behalf of the finance controller.
options.C: Summarising each completed questionnaire into a 5-point risk overview for the procurement lead.
options.D: Deciding which suppliers to approve based on risk score and relationship history.
options.E: Signing the master supplier agreement on behalf of the legal department.

items.question:
An insurance underwriter receives 600 commercial property renewal applications per month. A colleague argues this volume alone makes it a strong candidate for automated, Claude-assisted underwriting decisions. The underwriter pushes back.

Which argument BEST supports the underwriter's position?

options.A: 600 applications per month is not high enough volume to justify the cost of automation.
options.B: Insurance underwriting is categorically prohibited from AI involvement by regulation.
options.C: Claude performs better at underwriting tasks when given fewer applications at a time.
options.D: Volume is a necessary but not sufficient fit signal; each application requires complex risk judgement that varies materially by applicant history and property characteristics.

items.question:
An employee relations manager proposes using Claude to generate personalised performance improvement plan (PIP) letters for 30 employees, populated from structured HR data. The manager will review each letter before sending.

A compliance officer flags the design as carrying significant risk. What is the MOST likely basis for that concern?

options.A: Claude cannot access structured HR databases without a custom API integration.
options.B: Even with review, AI-generated PIP letters at volume may embed discriminatory language patterns that are difficult to detect during individual human review.
options.C: The manager reviewing each letter eliminates all meaningful risk from AI involvement in this process.
options.D: Generating 30 documents simultaneously exceeds Claude's practical output constraints.

items.question: A financial analyst is redesigning a quarterly earnings commentary workflow. Which THREE characteristics of a process step most strongly indicate it should remain a HUMAN step rather than be Claude-assisted? (Choose THREE)

options.A: The step requires interpreting ambiguous regulatory guidance with significant financial consequence.
options.B: The step applies a consistently defined formula to structured input data.
options.C: The step involves final sign-off that makes the output an official company statement.
options.D: The step requires synthesising non-public strategic context known only to senior leadership.
options.E: The step produces a draft that will be reviewed by a qualified colleague before release.

items.question:
A marketing operations manager plans to use Claude to personalise subject lines for 10,000 outbound emails using customer segment data. Her plan: (1) run all 10,000, (2) review a random sample of 50 outputs, (3) adjust the prompt if needed, (4) re-run if required.

A senior colleague recommends piloting on a small batch first. What is the BEST reason to run a small pilot BEFORE the full 10,000?

options.A: A prompt problem discovered after 10,000 outputs wastes all prior processing, and in some delivery models the messages may already have reached recipients before review is complete.
options.B: Claude's per-output accuracy declines when processing very large batches compared to small ones.
options.C: Email personalisation at this scale requires advance approval from the company's legal department.
options.D: A 50-message review sample is not statistically sufficient to approve the full run regardless of when it is conducted.
